name: OH-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: Deeply Republican district with a +21 Republican partisan lean
Jim Jordan is a well-funded, high-profile incumbent with $6 million on hand
Democratic challenger has raised under $13,000 with almost no cash remaining
Prediction markets price Jordan's win probability around 95%
model.rationale: This central Ohio seat is one of the most Republican districts in the country, and Jordan combines incumbency with a massive financial advantage over a challenger who has raised almost nothing. Markets and fundamentals both point to an easy Republican hold, with no polls or ratings suggesting any competitive threat.
model.watch: A surprise scandal or national wave election of historic magnitude would be the only realistic path to making this competitive.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Jim Jordan seeks another term in a district that leans about 21 points Republican, making this one of the safest Republican seats on the House map. He enters the general election with more than $6 million on hand after raising nearly $4.8 million, while Democratic nominee Joshua Kolasinski has raised under $13,000 and reports just a few hundred dollars in the bank. An independent candidate is also on the ballot but shows no measurable financial activity.

No public polling or expert ratings exist for this race, but prediction markets give Jordan roughly a 95 percent chance of winning, consistent with the district's fundamentals. The forecast expects Jordan to win by roughly 20 points, with the only meaningful uncertainty coming from turnout patterns in a low-salience race.
